text.p: German armaments maker Rheinmetall confirmed it would take over a 90 percent stake in Richard Hirschmann & Co GmbH effective January 1, 1997, according to a regulatory news release on Thursday.

The remaining 10 percent of the lossmaking takeover target will remain in the hands of the Hirschmann family. The news release confirmed an earlier report in the Stuttgarter Zeitung newspaper that a takeover was planned.
No price was named for the takeover, but Rheinmetall said that an injection of funds would help strengthen Hirschmann's equity capital.
The takeover has been approved by the Rheinmetall supervisory board, but awaits the all-clear from Hirschmann's board and German cartel authorities.

Hirschmann has annual turnover of 530 million marks and employs 2,800 workers. Its specialities are electrical and electronic products for speech, data and picture transmission in the vehicle, industry and communications sectors.
Rheinmetall recently led a consortium, which included British Aerospace, to buy defence electronics company STN Atlas -- a unit of bankrupt shipyard group Bremer Vulkan.
The company has also announced it plans to restructure at the end of the year, and will announce details on December 16.
